search: christopher wren christopher wren (1632 to 1723) was an english mathematician and astronomer, a founder of the royal society, who became an architect after the great fire of london in 1666. he designed more than fifty city churches and a new st paul's cathedral, topped out in 1708 and declared complete by parliament in 1711. wren was born in east knoyle, wiltshire, the son of a clergyman. he was appointed professor of astronomy at gresham college at 25, then savilian professor of astronomy at oxford, and was a founding member of the royal society in 1662. his architectural career began with the sheldonian theatre in oxford. the great fire of september 1666 destroyed old st paul's and most of the city. he was appointed surveyor of the king's works in 1669 and spent the rest of his working life on the city's parish churches and on st paul's. he died in 1723, aged 90, and is buried in the cathedral crypt. he combined the classical vocabulary of inigo jones and palladio with french and italian baroque elements he studied on a research trip to paris, the only time he travelled outside england. the dome of st paul's is three independent shells nested inside one another, so that exterior profile, interior ceiling and structural core could each be optimised separately. key works include the royal observatory, greenwich (1675 to 1676), the royal hospital chelsea (1682 to 1692) and the monument to the great fire (1671 to 1677). many city churches were later damaged or demolished, by victorian redevelopment and by german bombing, but a substantial number still stand. photographs of the dome above the smoke of the blitz in 1940 circulated worldwide.

title: Cixi
sum: The Empress Dowager Cixi (1835 to 1908) was the dominant political figure of late Qing China, ruling as regent for most of the period from 1861 to 1908.
search: cixi the empress dowager cixi (1835 to 1908) was the dominant political figure of late qing china, ruling as regent for most of the period from 1861 to 1908. she became regent in 1861 for her young son, the tongzhi emperor, and later for the guangxu emperor. her period includes the self-strengthening movement, an effort to modernize china's defenses and industry. she supported the boxers in 1900, and after their defeat she pursued the 'new policies' reforms. historians debate her legacy; older accounts portray her as a reactionary, and recent work stresses her political skill and the limits she faced.

title: Claude Monet
sum: Claude Monet (14 November 1840 to 5 December 1926) was a French painter, the leader and purest practitioner of Impressionism. His Impression, Sunrise gave the movement its name, and he spent his life painting the changing effects of light.
search: claude monet claude monet (14 november 1840 to 5 december 1926) was a french painter, the leader and purest practitioner of impressionism. his impression, sunrise gave the movement its name, and he spent his life painting the changing effects of light. monet was born in paris and grew up in le havre, where as a teenager he sold caricatures. eugène boudin persuaded him to paint outdoors. in paris he met camille pissarro and befriended renoir, sisley and bazille. the 1860s and 1870s were years of poverty. during the franco-prussian war he took refuge in london, where he saw turner's paintings and met the dealer paul durand-ruel. in 1874 he and his friends held an exhibition independent of the official salon. critics mocked them, and the name "impressionist" stuck. in 1883 his family settled at giverny in normandy, where he created a flower garden and a water garden with a japanese bridge, which became his main subject. he painted the same subject repeatedly in changing conditions: haystacks, poplars and rouen cathedral. key works include impression, sunrise (1872), stacks of wheat (1890 to 1891) and the water lilies. in his last decade he fought cataracts and worked on the giant grandes décorations, which he gave to the french state as a monument to peace after the first world war. he died at giverny. the abstract expressionists rediscovered his late water lilies in the 1950s. his house and gardens opened to the public in 1980, and in 2019 one of his haystacks sold for $110.7 million.

title: Cleopatra VII
sum: Cleopatra VII was the last active ruler of the Ptolemaic Kingdom of Egypt, who allied with Julius Caesar and Mark Antony and died in 30 BCE after their defeat by Octavian.
search: cleopatra vii cleopatra vii was the last active ruler of the ptolemaic kingdom of egypt, who allied with julius caesar and mark antony and died in 30 bce after their defeat by octavian. she belonged to the ptolemaic dynasty, founded by a macedonian general of alexander the great. ancient sources say she spoke several languages and, unlike most of her ptolemaic predecessors, learned egyptian. she had a son with julius caesar and children with mark antony. octavian defeated antony and cleopatra at the battle of actium in 31 bce. after her death in 30 bce, egypt became a roman province.

title: Confucius
sum: Confucius (Kong Fuzi, 551 to 479 BCE) was a Chinese teacher and thinker whose ideas about ethics, family, and government shaped East Asian societies for over two thousand years.
search: confucius confucius (kong fuzi, 551 to 479 bce) was a chinese teacher and thinker whose ideas about ethics, family, and government shaped east asian societies for over two thousand years. his sayings were collected by disciples in the analects. central ideas include ren (humaneness), li (ritual propriety), and filial piety. he was not widely influential during his lifetime; his ideas rose to prominence under the han dynasty. confucian learning later became the basis of the imperial civil service examinations.

title: Cyrus the Great
sum: Cyrus the Great founded the Achaemenid Persian Empire in the 6th century BCE by conquering the Medes, Lydia, and Babylon.
search: cyrus the great cyrus the great founded the achaemenid persian empire in the 6th century bce by conquering the medes, lydia, and babylon. his birth date is uncertain, with scholars giving about 600 to 576 bce. he defeated the median king astyages around 550 bce and the lydian king croesus around 547 bce. he took babylon in 539 bce. the cyrus cylinder, a babylonian clay cylinder found in 1879, records his account of the conquest and his restoration of gods and deported peoples. he died in 530 bce campaigning on the eastern frontier and was buried at pasargadae.

title: Darius I
sum: Darius I (about 550 to 486 BCE) was king of the Achaemenid Persian Empire from 522 BCE. He organized its provinces, began the building of Persepolis, and recorded his rise to power in the Behistun Inscription.
search: darius i darius i (about 550 to 486 bce) was king of the achaemenid persian empire from 522 bce. he organized its provinces, began the building of persepolis, and recorded his rise to power in the behistun inscription. darius i was born about 550 bce and became king in 522 bce after the death of cambyses ii. he put down revolts across the empire in his first years. the behistun inscription, carved on a cliff in western iran, tells the story of his rise in old persian, elamite and babylonian. scholars debate whether its account of a usurper, gaumata, is accurate, and aramaic copies of the text have been found in egypt. he divided the empire into provinces (satrapies) under governors and issued a standard gold coin, the daric. he is credited with the royal road from sardis to susa and began the terrace at persepolis about 518 bce, though sources differ and the earliest surviving remains there date to about 515 bce. his inscriptions honor the god ahura mazda. after the ionian greek cities revolted in 499 bce, he sent forces against athens, and the athenians defeated them at marathon in 490 bce. darius died in 486 bce and was succeeded by xerxes i.

title: Dido
sum: Dido, also called Elissa, is the legendary founder-queen of Carthage, traditionally said to have led Phoenician settlers from Tyre to found the city on the North African coast around 814 BCE; her birth and death dates are not historically…
search: dido dido, also called elissa, is the legendary founder-queen of carthage, traditionally said to have led phoenician settlers from tyre to found the city on the north african coast around 814 bce; her birth and death dates are not historically fixed. the earliest known account of her founding of carthage comes from the greek historian timaeus of tauromenium, writing in the 4th to 3rd century bce, centuries after the traditional founding date. tradition holds she fled tyre after her brother, king pygmalion, murdered her husband to seize his wealth, and that she later took her own life rather than marry a local libyan king, iarbas, who threatened war. no phoenician inscription or contemporary record names a founder called dido or elissa; archaeological evidence of phoenician settlement at the site of carthage has so far been found only from the last quarter of the 8th century bce, about a century or more after the traditional founding date, though it may still fit a folk memory of an organized colonizing expedition. her best-known appearance, as the doomed lover of the trojan hero aeneas in virgil's aeneid, is a literary invention: the trojan war's traditional date is centuries before carthage's traditional founding, so the two could not have met.

title: Diego Velázquez
sum: Diego Velázquez (1599 to 1660) was the leading painter of Spain's Golden Age and court painter to King Philip IV for 37 years. His loose, luminous brushwork and unflattering portraits of kings, courtiers and jesters made him a "painter's…
search: diego velázquez diego velázquez (1599 to 1660) was the leading painter of spain's golden age and court painter to king philip iv for 37 years. his loose, luminous brushwork and unflattering portraits of kings, courtiers and jesters made him a "painter's painter". velázquez was baptised in seville on 6 june 1599. at about 11 he entered the workshop of francisco pacheco, and in 1618 he married pacheco's daughter juana. his early seville work shows the influence of caravaggio. in 1623 a portrait of the young philip iv won him the post of court painter, and he moved to madrid. he rose through court offices to become chamberlain of the palace. peter paul rubens, on a diplomatic mission to madrid in 1628, encouraged him to visit italy. his first italian trip (1629 to 1631) transformed his colour and handling. a second (1649 to 1651) produced his portrait of pope innocent x. he painted las meninas in 1656 and in 1659 was admitted to the noble order of santiago, a rare honour for a painter. he died on 6 august 1660. he painted alla prima, often without drawing, and altered compositions on the canvas; x-rays reveal many changes of mind. his palette was restrained, built on greys, blacks and earth tones. his work stayed largely in spanish royal palaces until the prado opened in 1819. manet travelled to madrid in 1865 and called him "the painter of painters". picasso painted a series of 58 works on las meninas and related figures (1957), 44 of them variations on the whole painting, and francis bacon's screaming popes are based on his innocent x.

title: Edvard Munch

search: edvard munch edvard munch (12 december 1863 to 23 january 1944) was a norwegian painter and printmaker who turned illness, grief, love and fear into images of inner states. the scream became an emblem of the modern psyche, and he is a founding figure of expressionism. munch was born in løten, norway, and grew up in kristiania (now oslo). his mother died of tuberculosis when he was five and his sister sophie of the same disease when he was 13. another sister was later hospitalised for mental illness. in the 1890s he lived mostly in berlin and paris and developed the frieze of life cycle. his 1892 exhibition in berlin was closed after a week amid scandal, which made him famous in germany. he suffered a breakdown in 1908 and was treated in copenhagen. from 1916 he lived at his estate, ekely, outside oslo. in 1937 the nazis labelled his work "degenerate" and removed it from german museums. he simplified forms into flowing outlines and flat expressive colour, influenced by van gogh, gauguin and symbolism. his woodcuts and lithographs are as important as his paintings. key works include the sick child (1885 to 1886), the scream (1893), madonna (1894) and the dance of life (1899 to 1900). he left about 1,100 paintings, 4,500 drawings and 18,000 prints to the city of oslo. the scream has been stolen twice, in 1994 and 2004, and recovered both times.

title: Eleanor Roosevelt
sum: Eleanor Roosevelt (1884 to 1962) was First Lady of the United States from 1933 to 1945 and afterward a diplomat who chaired the United Nations commission that drafted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.
search: eleanor roosevelt eleanor roosevelt (1884 to 1962) was first lady of the united states from 1933 to 1945 and afterward a diplomat who chaired the united nations commission that drafted the universal declaration of human rights. she was born on 11 october 1884 in new york city and married franklin d. roosevelt in 1905. as first lady she redefined the role, holding her own press conferences, writing a daily newspaper column, and speaking for civil rights and the poor, sometimes publicly differing with her husband's policies. after his death in 1945, president truman appointed her a delegate to the new united nations in december 1945. she chaired the un commission on human rights, which drafted the universal declaration of human rights, adopted by the general assembly on 10 december 1948. she called this her greatest achievement. she later chaired a presidential commission on the status of women under president kennedy. she died on 7 november 1962 in new york city.

title: Eleanor of Aquitaine

search: eleanor of aquitaine eleanor of aquitaine (about 1124 to 1204, with older sources giving 1122 for her birth) was successively queen of france and queen of england, and one of the wealthiest and most powerful women in 12th-century europe as ruler of the duchy of aquitaine in her own right. she inherited the vast duchy of aquitaine in southwestern france in 1137 and married king louis vii of france that same year; the marriage was annulled in 1152 after producing no sons. weeks after the annulment she married henry of anjou, who became king henry ii of england in 1154, bringing her extensive french territories into the combined "angevin empire" that spanned much of france and england. she supported a rebellion by three of her sons against henry ii in 1173 to 1174; after its failure, henry kept her in confinement for about fifteen to sixteen years until his death in 1189. freed by her son richard i ("the lionheart"), she acted as regent during his crusade and captivity, and later helped secure the throne for her youngest son, john, after richard's death in 1199.

title: Emperor Meiji

title: Enheduanna
sum: Enheduanna (flourishing around 2300 BCE; the span of about 2285 to 2250 BCE is only an estimate) was a high priestess of the moon god Nanna at the Sumerian city of Ur and a daughter of Sargon of Akkad. She is often called the earliest…
search: enheduanna enheduanna (flourishing around 2300 bce; the span of about 2285 to 2250 bce is only an estimate) was a high priestess of the moon god nanna at the sumerian city of ur and a daughter of sargon of akkad. she is often called the earliest author known by name, though her dates and the attribution of her texts are debated. enheduanna served as en-priestess of nanna at ur, appointed by her father sargon of akkad. her dates depend on the chronology used. a disc found at ur in 1927 by leonard woolley's team shows a figure identified by inscription as enheduanna, daughter of sargon, in a ritual scene. sumerian poems are attributed to her, including 42 temple hymns and hymns to the goddess inanna such as "the exaltation of inanna." the surviving copies come from schools of the old babylonian period, about 1800 bce, some five to six centuries after her lifetime, and scholars disagree about whether she wrote every attributed text. in "the exaltation of inanna" the speaker describes being driven from office by a usurper, lugal-ane, and restored; the historicity of this is debated.

title: Ezana of Aksum

search: ezana of aksum ezana was king of aksum, in present-day ethiopia and eritrea, from about 320 to about 360 ce, though sources differ on the exact dates. he is known for adopting christianity and for a campaign in the nile valley, and his inscriptions and coins record both. ezana came to the throne as a child and ruled the kingdom of aksum from about 320 until about 360. dates for his life and reign are approximate, and sources differ. his early inscriptions and coins show older aksumite religion, including a crescent and disc on his coins. frumentius, a christian from tyre (described as phoenician, and in some accounts syrian) who rose in the aksumite court, is reported to have been consecrated aksum's first bishop by athanasius of alexandria, traditionally in 328, though other accounts say between 340 and 346. ezana converted to christianity in the 4th century, though the exact date is uncertain. his later inscriptions invoke a "lord of heaven," and his coins replace the crescent and disc with the cross, which is often described as among the earliest coins to do so. his inscriptions are in ge'ez, sabaean and greek. about 350 an aksumite force campaigned in the nile valley against kush and neighboring peoples. the campaign is often linked to the end of kush's power, though historians debate the causes.

title: Francisco Goya
sum: Francisco Goya (30 March 1746 to 16 April 1828) was a Spanish court painter and printmaker, often called the last of the Old Masters and the first of the moderns. Illness, political repression and the Napoleonic invasion drove him from…
search: francisco goya francisco goya (30 march 1746 to 16 april 1828) was a spanish court painter and printmaker, often called the last of the old masters and the first of the moderns. illness, political repression and the napoleonic invasion drove him from brilliant royal portraits toward satire, violence and the irrational. goya was born in fuendetodos in aragon and grew up in zaragoza. in 1773 he married josefa bayeu, sister of the court painter francisco bayeu, who helped him win work designing tapestry cartoons in madrid. by 1786 he was painter to the king, and in 1799 first court painter to charles iv. in 1792 to 1793 an illness left him permanently deaf. in 1799 he published los caprichos, satirical etchings mocking superstition and the clergy. when napoleon's armies invaded spain in 1808 he witnessed atrocities on both sides and recorded them in the disasters of war, prints published only 35 years after his death. he painted the second and third of may 1808 in 1814. disillusioned by the repressive rule of ferdinand vii, he retreated to a house outside madrid and covered its walls with the black paintings, including saturn devouring his son (1819 to 1823). in 1824 he went into exile in bordeaux, where he died. his portraits, influenced by velázquez, use loose brushwork and avoid flattery. he mastered aquatint for deep shadows and later applied paint with knives, rags and fingers. goya named rembrandt as one of his three masters. manet's execution of emperor maximilian and picasso's guernica both descend from the third of may. the prado holds the greatest collection of his work.

title: Frank Lloyd Wright
sum: Frank Lloyd Wright (1867 to 1959) was the most influential American architect of the 20th century. Over seven decades he argued for "organic architecture", buildings designed from the inside out around their site, materials and users.
search: frank lloyd wright frank lloyd wright (1867 to 1959) was the most influential american architect of the 20th century. over seven decades he argued for "organic architecture", buildings designed from the inside out around their site, materials and users. wright was born in richland center, wisconsin, studied engineering briefly at the university of wisconsin and moved to chicago, where he worked under louis sullivan, whom he later called his "lieber meister". he set up his own practice in oak park in the 1890s and developed the low, wide-eaved prairie house style. his personal life was turbulent: an affair, the killing of seven people at his wisconsin home taliesin in 1914, and bankruptcy during the depression. in his late sixties he designed fallingwater and the johnson wax headquarters (both 1936 to 1939), and finally the guggenheim museum (design and construction from 1943 to 1959). he died in 1959 aged 91. he designed around open, flowing interior space, with art-glass bands and deep cantilevered overhangs, and used concrete, steel and glass without disguising them as historical stonework. he designed most of the furniture, textiles and stained glass in his buildings himself. he designed more than a thousand structures, roughly half built. fallingwater and several others are a unesco world heritage site. late in life he planned an unrealised city, broadacre city, of low-density, car-based suburban living. he was also a major collector and dealer of hiroshige's prints.

title: Frederick Barbarossa
sum: Frederick I, called Barbarossa ("Redbeard"; about 1122 to 1190), was Holy Roman Emperor from 1155 until his death, and one of medieval Europe's most powerful rulers, spending much of his reign contesting control of northern Italy.
search: frederick barbarossa frederick i, called barbarossa ("redbeard"; about 1122 to 1190), was holy roman emperor from 1155 until his death, and one of medieval europe's most powerful rulers, spending much of his reign contesting control of northern italy. elected king of germany in 1152, he was crowned holy roman emperor by the pope in 1155, and repeatedly invaded italy to assert imperial authority over its wealthy independent city-states. the lombard league, an alliance of northern italian cities backed by the papacy, defeated his forces at the battle of legnano in 1176, forcing him to recognize significant city autonomy in the peace of constance of 1183. he arranged the marriage of his son henry to constance of sicily, a match that later brought the kingdom of sicily under his family's control. he drowned in 1190 while crossing a river in anatolia during the third crusade, before reaching the holy land; his death caused much of his army to disband or turn back rather than continue the campaign.

title: Frida Kahlo
sum: Frida Kahlo (1907 to 1954) was a Mexican painter, best known for small, vivid self-portraits made in Mexico City. She worked through years of pain after a bus accident in 1925 and became a global cultural icon after her death.
search: frida kahlo frida kahlo (1907 to 1954) was a mexican painter, best known for small, vivid self-portraits made in mexico city. she worked through years of pain after a bus accident in 1925 and became a global cultural icon after her death. kahlo was born on 6 july 1907 in coyoacán, now part of mexico city. she often gave 1910, the year the mexican revolution began, as her birth year. a bus accident on 17 september 1925 broke her spine, pelvis and right leg and ended her plan to study medicine. she began painting during her recovery. she married the muralist diego rivera in 1929, divorced him in 1939 and remarried him in 1940. estimates of her output run from fewer than 150 to about 200 paintings, most of them self-portraits, including the two fridas (1939) and the broken column (1944). her first solo show was at the julien levy gallery in new york in 1938. in 1939 the louvre bought her painting the frame, the first work by a mexican artist in its collection. she died in mexico city on 13 july 1954, officially of a pulmonary embolism. her work was little known until art historians rediscovered it in the late 1970s.

title: Fu Hao
sum: Fu Hao (died about 1200 BCE) was a consort of the Shang king Wu Ding, named in oracle bone inscriptions as a military commander and a ritual leader. Her intact tomb, found in 1976, is among the richest of the Shang period. Her birth year…
search: fu hao fu hao (died about 1200 bce) was a consort of the shang king wu ding, named in oracle bone inscriptions as a military commander and a ritual leader. her intact tomb, found in 1976, is among the richest of the shang period. her birth year is unknown. fu hao is named in oracle bone inscriptions as a wife of the shang king wu ding, whose reign is dated about 1250 to 1192 bce, though dates vary by chronology. she is thought to have died about 1200 bce. the inscriptions record her leading military campaigns against neighboring groups and directing ritual sacrifices. her tomb (m5) at yinxu, the shang capital site near anyang in henan, was found undisturbed in 1976 by a team led by zheng zhenxiang. it held 468 bronze objects and 755 jade objects, as well as hundreds of bone objects and thousands of cowry shells. inscriptions on many bronzes name her, fu hao, or "mother xin," which is the basis for identifying the tomb with the woman of the oracle bones. sixteen people and six dogs were buried with her, interpreted as sacrifices.

title: Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti
sum: Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti (1900 to 1978) was a Nigerian teacher and campaigner who led the Abeokuta Women's Union in protests against a tax on women and against the local ruler, the Alake of Egbaland, in the 1940s.
search: funmilayo ransome-kuti funmilayo ransome-kuti (1900 to 1978) was a nigerian teacher and campaigner who led the abeokuta women's union in protests against a tax on women and against the local ruler, the alake of egbaland, in the 1940s. funmilayo ransome-kuti was born on 25 october 1900 in abeokuta, in southwestern nigeria. she studied there and in cheshire, england, from 1919 to 1922. in 1925 she married the reverend israel oludotun ransome-kuti. their children included the musician fela kuti and the physicians beko and olikoye ransome-kuti. she founded the abeokuta ladies' club in 1932. it became the abeokuta women's union about 1946 and is reported to have had about 20,000 members. in the late 1940s the union protested a tax on women and the rule of the alake, ademola ii, who was forced to leave the throne for a time in 1949. she helped found the federation of nigerian women's societies in 1953 and received the lenin peace prize in 1970. on 18 february 1977 soldiers stormed her son's compound in lagos. her family says she was thrown from an upper-floor window, and she died of her injuries on 13 april 1978. official accounts blamed unknown soldiers.

title: Galileo Galilei
sum: Galileo Galilei (1564 to 1642) was an Italian scientist who used the telescope and experiments to support the Copernican view that the Earth orbits the Sun.
search: galileo galilei galileo galilei (1564 to 1642) was an italian scientist who used the telescope and experiments to support the copernican view that the earth orbits the sun. in 1609 and 1610 he observed the moon's mountains and four moons of jupiter. he studied falling bodies and motion using experiments. in 1633 the roman inquisition tried him and he was placed under house arrest for the rest of his life. his 'dialogue concerning the two chief world systems' was published in 1632.

title: Genghis Khan
sum: Genghis Khan (born Temujin, about 1162 to 1227) united the Mongol tribes in 1206 and founded the Mongol Empire.
search: genghis khan genghis khan (born temujin, about 1162 to 1227) united the mongol tribes in 1206 and founded the mongol empire. he built an army based on merit and loyalty rather than clan. his campaigns overran central asia, northern china, and persia. he promoted a written script and a legal code (the yassa) and encouraged religious tolerance. he died in 1227; the location of his tomb is unknown.

title: Georges Méliès
sum: Georges Méliès (1861 to 1938) was a Paris stage magician who became a filmmaker and invented cinema's first special effects. Over roughly 500 films in under twenty years, including A Trip to the Moon (1902), he turned the new camera from a…
search: georges méliès georges méliès (1861 to 1938) was a paris stage magician who became a filmmaker and invented cinema's first special effects. over roughly 500 films in under twenty years, including a trip to the moon (1902), he turned the new camera from a device for recording reality into a machine for staging the impossible. méliès was born in paris to a prosperous shoe-manufacturing family and wanted to study painting, but his father would not support him as an artist and he supervised machinery at the family factory. in about 1888 he bought the théâtre robert-houdin, a famous conjuring theatre. after attending the lumière brothers' first public film screening in december 1895, he tried to buy a camera from them and was refused. he acquired one from a british inventor and built a studio at montreuil with a glass-walled stage. about 1896 he discovered, by accident when his camera jammed mid-shot, that stopping and restarting filming could make objects vanish or transform. this became the "stop trick" behind his trick films. his techniques included stop-motion substitution, multiple exposure, dissolves, painted sets built to force perspective, and hand-tinted colour done frame by frame by a team of women colourists. american piracy of his films, the rise of narrative studio filmmaking and the disruption of the first world war ruined his business. he was reduced to running a toy stall in a paris train station. he was rediscovered in his last decade, awarded the légion d'honneur and, by some accounts, given a small pension. he died in paris in 1938. martin scorsese's 2011 film hugo dramatised his life. key works include the vanishing lady (1896), a trip to the moon (1902), the kingdom of the fairies (1903) and the impossible voyage (1904).

title: Gilgamesh

search: gilgamesh gilgamesh was a king of the sumerian city of uruk, probably a real ruler of the early dynastic period sometime between about 2800 and 2500 bce, who became the subject of the epic of gilgamesh, the earliest surviving major work of narrative literature. the sumerian king list names him as the fifth king of uruk's first dynasty and credits him with an implausible 126-year reign, typical of the list's treatment of early rulers. later inscriptions, notably the tummal inscription written under ishbi-erra long after the early dynastic period, credit a king of this name with building the great city walls of uruk, a claim the epic itself repeats as gilgamesh's lasting achievement. the epic, assembled from older sumerian poems into its best-known akkadian version around the 12th century bce, follows gilgamesh's friendship with the wild man enkidu, his quest for immortality after enkidu's death, and his eventual acceptance of mortality. no securely contemporary royal inscription from gilgamesh's own lifetime has been found, though one inscription possibly from a contemporary official at ur may name him; most of what historians infer about a real gilgamesh comes from later king lists, dedicatory inscriptions naming him, and the literary tradition itself.

title: Giotto
sum: Giotto di Bondone (about 1267 to 1337) was a Florentine painter who gave medieval figures weight, emotion and space. Many call him the father of Western painting, and his frescoes in the Scrovegni Chapel in Padua are his firmest work.
search: giotto giotto di bondone (about 1267 to 1337) was a florentine painter who gave medieval figures weight, emotion and space. many call him the father of western painting, and his frescoes in the scrovegni chapel in padua are his firmest work. giotto was born about 1267, traditionally in the mugello valley north of florence, though his birthplace is disputed and some recent research points to florence itself. vasari's story of the shepherd boy discovered by cimabue is legend, but he was almost certainly trained in florentine workshops. he was traditionally credited with the legend of st francis frescoes at assisi in the late 1290s, but it is now generally accepted that four different hands are identifiable there and that they came from rome, so his authorship is doubtful; his early career is still debated. he painted the scrovegni chapel in padua about 1303 to 1305 for the banker enrico scrovegni. it is now a unesco world heritage site. he worked in rome, in santa croce in florence, and at the court of king robert of anjou in naples from about 1328 to 1333. in 1334 florence named him master of works for the cathedral, and he designed its bell tower. he died in january 1337 and was buried with public honours. he worked in buon fresco, painting into wet plaster one day's section at a time. his figures have volume and react to one another, and his spaces suggest depth more than 100 years before linear perspective was worked out. in the chapel's adoration of the magi the star is painted as a blazing comet, perhaps inspired by halley's comet of 1301. the european space agency named its 1986 halley probe giotto. vasari opened his lives of the artists with cimabue and giotto. masaccio and  michelangelo  studied and copied giotto's frescoes.

title: Gitarja
sum: Tribhuwana Wijayatunggadewi, known as Gitarja, was the third monarch of the Majapahit empire, reigning in Java from about 1328 to 1350; her birth is placed before 1309 and her death about 1372 to 1375, though both dates are uncertain.
search: gitarja tribhuwana wijayatunggadewi, known as gitarja, was the third monarch of the majapahit empire, reigning in java from about 1328 to 1350; her birth is placed before 1309 and her death about 1372 to 1375, though both dates are uncertain. she became queen after the assassination of her half-brother jayanegara in 1328 (the nagarakretagama gives 1329 for her accession), ruling in the name of her mother, gayatri rajapatni, who had formally retired to a buddhist convent. her chief minister, gajah mada, is credited with a famous oath to abstain from certain pleasures until he had brought the surrounding archipelago under majapahit's authority. under her reign majapahit forces conquered bali in 1343, defeating the kingdoms of pejeng and bedahulu, a major step in the empire's expansion across the indonesian archipelago. she stepped down in 1350 after her mother's death and was succeeded by her son, hayam wuruk, under whom majapahit reached its greatest territorial extent.

title: Gorgo
sum: Gorgo (born about 518 BCE, last attested around 480 BCE) was queen of Sparta as the wife of King Leonidas I, remembered by the historian Herodotus as unusually sharp-witted and politically perceptive for a woman in his account of Greek…
search: gorgo gorgo (born about 518 bce, last attested around 480 bce) was queen of sparta as the wife of king leonidas i, remembered by the historian herodotus as unusually sharp-witted and politically perceptive for a woman in his account of greek affairs. she was the daughter of the spartan king cleomenes i and, according to herodotus, advised him as a child not to trust a bribe offered by an ionian envoy seeking spartan military aid. herodotus credits her with detecting a warning about the persian king xerxes's invasion plans hidden on a wax-covered writing tablet sent by the exiled spartan king demaratus, when other spartans could not work out its message. she was the wife of leonidas i, who died leading the defense of thermopylae against the persian invasion in 480 bce, the same year in which she is last clearly attested in the sources. nearly everything known of her comes from herodotus's histories, written decades after her lifetime, and no independent spartan record of her actions survives.

title: Gustav Klimt
sum: Gustav Klimt (14 July 1862 to 6 February 1918) was an Austrian painter and the leader of the Vienna Secession. His golden, patterned paintings of women and love, above all The Kiss, are icons of turn-of-the-century Vienna.
search: gustav klimt gustav klimt (14 july 1862 to 6 february 1918) was an austrian painter and the leader of the vienna secession. his golden, patterned paintings of women and love, above all the kiss, are icons of turn-of-the-century vienna. klimt was born at baumgarten near vienna, the second of seven children of a gold engraver. he won a scholarship to the vienna school of arts and crafts in 1876 and, with his brother ernst and franz matsch, painted murals and ceilings for the burgtheater and the kunsthistorisches museum. in 1897 he became the first president of the vienna secession, a group breaking from the official academy with the motto "to every age its art, to art its freedom". his ceiling paintings for the university of vienna, showing philosophy, medicine and jurisprudence, caused a scandal over nudity and pessimism. he withdrew from the commission, and the paintings were destroyed in a fire in 1945. he never married, had a lifelong companionship with the designer emilie flöge and fathered several children with models. he supported younger artists such as egon schiele and oskar kokoschka. he died in vienna after a stroke. in his "golden period" (about 1899 to 1910) he applied real gold and silver leaf, drawing on byzantine mosaics he saw in ravenna in 1903, and on japanese and egyptian art. key works include the kiss (1907 to 1908) and the portrait of adele bloch-bauer i (1907). many of his works were owned by jewish collectors and looted by the nazis. the return of the adele bloch-bauer portrait to maria altmann made headlines worldwide. ronald lauder bought it in 2006 for a reported $135 million. in 2023 lady with a fan sold for £85.3 million, a record for a painting at auction in europe.

title: Hammurabi
sum: Hammurabi was the king of Babylon from about 1792 to 1750 BCE, who united much of Mesopotamia and is known for a famous inscribed law code.

title: Harald Hardrada
sum: Harald Hardrada (about 1015 to 1066) was King of Norway from 1046 to 1066, a warrior-king whose career took him from exile through mercenary service in Byzantium to the throne, and whose death at Stamford Bridge is often used to mark the…

title: Harriet Tubman
sum: Harriet Tubman (about 1822 to 1913) was an American abolitionist who escaped slavery in Maryland in 1849 and then guided others to freedom on the Underground Railroad. She later served the Union Army in the Civil War.
search: harriet tubman harriet tubman (about 1822 to 1913) was an american abolitionist who escaped slavery in maryland in 1849 and then guided others to freedom on the underground railroad. she later served the union army in the civil war. tubman was born araminta ross into slavery in dorchester county, maryland; her birth year is uncertain, with sources giving dates from 1815 to 1825 and about 1822 the most favoured. as a teenager she suffered a severe head injury when an overseer threw a metal weight, and had seizures and headaches for the rest of her life. she escaped to pennsylvania in 1849 and afterward made about 13 trips back to maryland, guiding roughly 70 people to freedom, according to her biographers. during the civil war she served the union army as a cook, nurse, scout and spy. in june 1863 she helped guide the combahee river raid in south carolina, which freed more than 700 enslaved people, though some sources give more than 750. after the war she lived in auburn, new york, where she cared for her family and for elderly people, and she worked for women's suffrage. she died in auburn on 10 march 1913.

title: Hatshepsut

search: hatshepsut hatshepsut was an egyptian ruler of the 18th dynasty who held the title of pharaoh, sharing the throne with thutmose iii, until her death in 1458 bce. her reign is traditionally dated 1479 to 1458 bce, and she is one of the first women known to have held the office. she first acted as regent for her young stepson thutmose iii, then took the title of pharaoh around the seventh year of his reign (about 1473 bce), sharing his regnal count. she sponsored a trading expedition to punt, on the red sea coast of africa. her mortuary temple at deir el-bahari is a major monument. many of her images were later removed or defaced, possibly after her death.

title: Henry Ossawa Tanner
sum: Henry Ossawa Tanner (21 June 1859 to 25 May 1937) was an American painter, the first African American artist to win international fame. Frustrated by racism at home, he settled in Paris in 1891 and built his career there, painting…
search: henry ossawa tanner henry ossawa tanner (21 june 1859 to 25 may 1937) was an american painter, the first african american artist to win international fame. frustrated by racism at home, he settled in paris in 1891 and built his career there, painting dignified genre scenes and luminous biblical subjects. tanner was born in pittsburgh, the eldest of nine children. his father, benjamin tucker tanner, became a bishop of the african methodist episcopal church, and his mother, sarah, had escaped slavery via the underground railroad. at 13 he decided to become an artist. in 1879 he enrolled at the pennsylvania academy of the fine arts and studied with thomas eakins. he was the only black student and faced harassment. he left for europe in 1891 and studied at the académie julian in paris. on a return visit in 1893 he painted the banjo lesson, and he painted the thankful poor in 1894, both genre scenes of black american life that challenged racist stereotypes. back in france he turned to biblical subjects. the resurrection of lazarus won a medal at the 1897 salon, and the french government bought it. his patron rodman wanamaker paid for trips to egypt and palestine. he married the singer jessie olsson in 1899. he was made a chevalier of the légion d'honneur in 1923 and died in paris. he preferred a limited palette of deep blues and blue-greens with glowing gold highlights, built up in layers of glaze. he advised younger painters such as william edouard scott and hale woodruff, and was a hero to the artists of the harlem renaissance. during the clinton administration, reportedly in 1996, his sand dunes at sunset, atlantic city became the first painting by an african american artist in the white house collection.

title: Hieronymus Bosch
sum: Hieronymus Bosch (about 1450 to 1516) was a painter from 's-Hertogenbosch in the Duchy of Brabant who filled his panels with hybrid monsters and crowds of tiny figures acting out human sin and folly. Only about 25 paintings are firmly…
search: hieronymus bosch hieronymus bosch (about 1450 to 1516) was a painter from 's-hertogenbosch in the duchy of brabant who filled his panels with hybrid monsters and crowds of tiny figures acting out human sin and folly. only about 25 paintings are firmly attributed to him. bosch was born jheronimus van aken about 1450 in 's-hertogenbosch. his grandfather, father and uncles were painters, and he later signed his works "jheronimus bosch" after the town. sometime between 1479 and 1481 he married aleid goyaerts van den meervenne, of a wealthy family. in 1486 or 1487 he became a sworn member of the illustrious brotherhood of our blessed lady, and he died in 1516. he seems to have spent almost his whole life in and near 's-hertogenbosch, and after marrying he and aleid moved to nearby oirschot, yet his fame spread. philip the handsome, duke of burgundy, commissioned a last judgment from him in 1504. he painted in oil on oak panels, often as triptychs. key works include the garden of earthly delights (about 1495 to 1505), the ship of fools (about 1500 to 1510), the temptation of st anthony (about 1501) and the haywain triptych (about 1510 to 1516). king philip ii of spain acquired many bosch paintings in the late 16th century, which is why the prado in madrid holds his greatest paintings.  pieter bruegel the elder  built on his crowded moral landscapes. after being partly forgotten, bosch was claimed in the 20th century by surrealists such as salvador dalí and max ernst. in 2016, the 500th anniversary of his death, the bosch research and conservation project re-examined his works, and several attributions changed in both directions, with a temptation of st anthony credited to bosch himself after being given to his workshop, and other works questioned as workshop pieces.

title: Indira Gandhi
