search: indira gandhi indira gandhi (1917 to 1984) was prime minister of india for most of 1966 to 1984. she led india through the 1971 war that created bangladesh, imposed emergency rule from 1975 to 1977, and was assassinated by her own bodyguards after ordering an army raid on sikhism's holiest shrine. she was born on 19 november 1917 in allahabad, daughter of jawaharlal nehru, india's first prime minister, and became prime minister herself in 1966. in 1971 india backed the independence of east pakistan, which became bangladesh, after a short war with pakistan. on 25 june 1975 she had a state of emergency declared, suspending civil liberties, censoring the press and jailing opponents, until elections in 1977 that she lost. she returned to power in 1980. government policy also pushed the green revolution's higher-yield crops during her years in office. in june 1984 she ordered operation blue star, a military assault on the golden temple in amritsar to remove armed sikh militants, which damaged the shrine and angered many sikhs. on 31 october 1984 two of her sikh bodyguards assassinated her in new delhi. riots afterward killed thousands of sikhs, mostly in delhi.

title: Isaac Newton
sum: Isaac Newton (1642 to 1727) was an English mathematician and physicist whose laws of motion and universal gravitation formed the basis of classical mechanics.
search: isaac newton isaac newton (1642 to 1727) was an english mathematician and physicist whose laws of motion and universal gravitation formed the basis of classical mechanics. his 'principia' (1687) presents the laws of motion and the law of gravitation. he developed calculus, independently of leibniz, leading to a priority dispute. he studied optics, showing that white light is composed of colors. he also spent much time on alchemy and theology.

title: J. M. W. Turner
sum: Joseph Mallord William Turner (April 1775 to 19 December 1851) was the greatest British landscape painter and a bold colourist. He began as a precise topographical watercolourist, and his late paintings dissolve ships, trains and cities…
search: j. m. w. turner joseph mallord william turner (april 1775 to 19 december 1851) was the greatest british landscape painter and a bold colourist. he began as a precise topographical watercolourist, and his late paintings dissolve ships, trains and cities into light, mist and weather. turner was born in covent garden, london, the son of a barber and wigmaker. at 14 he entered the royal academy schools and at 15 exhibited his first watercolour. he was elected a full royal academician in 1802, at 26 or 27 depending on the source. he travelled tirelessly in britain, the alps, france, germany and italy, especially venice, filling hundreds of sketchbooks. he never married but had two daughters with sarah danby. john ruskin championed him in modern painters (1843). he died in chelsea and was buried in st paul's cathedral. by the 1830s he painted natural forces themselves, storms, fire, sunlight and steam. he worked thin washes over white grounds, scraped and rubbed his canvases, and applied paint thickly with knives. he painted steamships and railways alongside venetian lagoons. rain, steam and speed (1844) is one of the first great paintings of modern technology. the slave ship (1840) was possibly inspired by the zong massacre of 1781, when enslaved africans were thrown overboard so owners could claim insurance. he showed it during the 1840 campaign to end slavery worldwide. he left around 300 oil paintings and over 19,000 sketches, drawings and watercolours and some 200 sketchbooks to the nation, held mainly at tate britain. monet and pissarro studied his work in london in 1870 to 1871, and the turner prize has been awarded since 1984.

title: Jadwiga
sum: Jadwiga (about 1373 to 1399) was crowned "King" of Poland in 1384 at about age ten, often described as the first woman to rule Poland in her own right, and her marriage to the Grand Duke of Lithuania began a dynastic union between the two…
search: jadwiga jadwiga (about 1373 to 1399) was crowned "king" of poland in 1384 at about age ten, often described as the first woman to rule poland in her own right, and her marriage to the grand duke of lithuania began a dynastic union between the two states. she was crowned using the male title "rex" (king) rather than "regina" (queen) to underscore that she held full sovereign authority in her own right, not merely as a royal consort. in 1386 she married jogaila, the pagan grand duke of lithuania, who converted to christianity and was crowned co-ruler as wladyslaw ii jagiello, founding the jagiellonian dynasty and beginning the christianization of lithuania. she helped fund the restoration of the krakow academy, later the jagiellonian university, through jewellery donated and, under her will, sold to help finance it, helping revive an institution that became a major center of learning in central europe. she died in 1399, about three and a half weeks after giving birth to a daughter who also died in infancy, four days before her, ending her direct line; she was canonized by the catholic church in 1997.

title: Jan van Eyck
sum: Jan van Eyck (born about 1380 or 1390, died 1441) was the leading painter of the Burgundian Netherlands and a founder of Early Netherlandish painting. He refined a method of thin, translucent oil glazes that let him paint light and texture…
search: jan van eyck jan van eyck (born about 1380 or 1390, died 1441) was the leading painter of the burgundian netherlands and a founder of early netherlandish painting. he refined a method of thin, translucent oil glazes that let him paint light and texture with unprecedented realism. van eyck was probably born sometime around 1380 or 1390 near maaseik, in present-day belgian limburg. nothing is known of his training. he appears in records about 1422 at the hague, working for john of bavaria. from 1425 he was court painter and valet de chambre to philip the good, duke of burgundy, who sent him on confidential missions, including a trip to portugal in 1428 to 1429 to paint princess isabella. about 1430 he settled in bruges. he completed the ghent altarpiece, begun by his brother hubert, in 1432, and died in bruges in july 1441. he did not invent oil paint, as vasari later claimed. he built up many thin, transparent glazes, and he often signed and dated his work, sometimes with the motto als ich can ("as i can"). key works include the ghent altarpiece (1432), the arnolfini portrait (1434) and the madonna of chancellor rolin (about 1435). he did not use the mathematical perspective being developed in italy. he built space through observation of light and atmosphere. the ghent altarpiece survived iconoclasm, fire and napoleon's looters, was seized by the nazis, and was recovered from an austrian salt mine. a restoration begun in 2012 revealed the lamb's strikingly human face in 2020.

title: Jane Austen
sum: Jane Austen (1775 to 1817) was an English novelist whose six completed novels of courtship, inheritance and class anxiety among the gentry remain among the most widely read in the language. All were published anonymously in her lifetime.
search: jane austen jane austen (1775 to 1817) was an english novelist whose six completed novels of courtship, inheritance and class anxiety among the gentry remain among the most widely read in the language. all were published anonymously in her lifetime. austen was born in 1775 in steventon, hampshire, the seventh of eight children of a country clergyman, in a family that encouraged reading, amateur theatre and writing. sense and sensibility appeared in 1811, credited only to "a lady", followed by pride and prejudice (1813), mansfield park (1814), emma (1815) and, after her death, northanger abbey and persuasion (1817). only close family knew of her authorship. she fell ill, probably with addison's disease though the cause is debated, and died in 1817 at 41. her authorship was publicly acknowledged in a biographical notice her brother attached to her last two novels. she worked within a deliberately narrow social canvas, mainly the english gentry, courtship, income and inheritance, rather than the wider political events of her era. her distinctive technique is free indirect discourse: narrating in the third person while letting the prose absorb a character's own irony or blind spots, so the reader senses a character's error before the character does. her novels have remained continuously in print and are widely adapted for film, television and stage. her reputation grew after her death rather than during her modest anonymous success.

title: Jayavarman VII
sum: Jayavarman VII (about 1122 to about 1218) was king of the Khmer Empire from about 1181 until his death. He drove out Cham invaders who had sacked Angkor and then led a large building program that included Angkor Thom and the Bayon.
search: jayavarman vii jayavarman vii (about 1122 to about 1218) was king of the khmer empire from about 1181 until his death. he drove out cham invaders who had sacked angkor and then led a large building program that included angkor thom and the bayon. champa forces sacked angkor in 1177. jayavarman vii defeated them and was crowned about 1181; his birth and death years are estimates. khmer forces later brought parts of champa under khmer control. he was a mahayana buddhist, while most earlier khmer rulers had favored hindu cults. his projects include angkor thom, the bayon with its towers carved with large faces, ta prohm (dedicated to his mother) and preah khan (dedicated to his father). an inscription of 1186 at ta prohm credits him with 102 hospitals; the figure comes from the king's own inscriptions. the faces on the bayon towers are variously read as a buddhist deity, the king, or both.

title: Jeong Seon
sum: Jeong Seon (1676 to 1759), pen name Gyeomjae, was a Korean painter of the Joseon dynasty who transformed landscape painting by depicting the real scenery of Korea instead of imagined Chinese scenery. His "true-view landscape" (jingyeong…
search: jeong seon jeong seon (1676 to 1759), pen name gyeomjae, was a korean painter of the joseon dynasty who transformed landscape painting by depicting the real scenery of korea instead of imagined chinese scenery. his "true-view landscape" (jingyeong sansuhwa) expressed a growing pride in korean culture. jeong seon was born in 1676 in hanyang (modern seoul), into a scholarly family of modest means. his father died when he was young. he trained in painting and in neo-confucian learning. through recommendations he held government posts, including county magistrate at hayang and yangcheon, and rose to high official rank in old age. he lived near mount inwang in seoul. his friend the poet yi byeong-yeon exchanged poems and paintings with him for decades. in 1711 and 1712 he travelled to the diamond mountains (geumgangsan), and the albums he made there made his name. he died in 1759 at 83. for centuries korean painters had followed chinese models. he painted the actual scenery of korea and invented his own brushstrokes: sharp vertical strokes for granite peaks and soft wet dots for forested earth mountains. he often combined a bird's-eye view with exaggeration. his paintings are not maps but expressions of the experience of real places. two works, geumgang jeondo and inwang jesaekdo, are national treasures of south korea. kim hong-do and sim sa-jeong followed him, and the gyeomjae jeong seon art museum opened in seoul in 2009.

title: Johannes Gutenberg
sum: Johannes Gutenberg (about 1400 to 1468) was a German metalworker who developed a movable-type printing press in Mainz around 1440 and printed the Gutenberg Bible about 1455.
search: johannes gutenberg johannes gutenberg (about 1400 to 1468) was a german metalworker who developed a movable-type printing press in mainz around 1440 and printed the gutenberg bible about 1455. he combined metal type, oil-based ink, and a press adapted from wine-making. the 42-line bible is the earliest major book printed from movable type in europe. he faced financial difficulties and lost control of his workshop to a creditor. printing spread rapidly across europe within decades.

title: Johannes Vermeer
sum: Johannes Vermeer (1632 to 1675) was a painter of Delft in the Dutch Republic. About 35 paintings are accepted as his, mostly quiet interiors lit by daylight from a window. Almost forgotten for 200 years after his death, he is now among the…
search: johannes vermeer johannes vermeer (1632 to 1675) was a painter of delft in the dutch republic. about 35 paintings are accepted as his, mostly quiet interiors lit by daylight from a window. almost forgotten for 200 years after his death, he is now among the most famous painters in the world. vermeer was baptised in delft on 31 october 1632. his father was a silk weaver who also dealt in art and ran an inn. nothing is known of vermeer's training. in 1653 he married catharina bolnes, a catholic from a wealthier family, and probably converted. the same year he joined delft's guild of st luke, which later elected him one of its leaders several times. the couple lived with catharina's mother and had 15 children, 11 of whom survived. he also worked as an art dealer, and his slow output was bought largely by one local patron, pieter van ruijven. in 1672, the dutch republic's "disaster year", france invaded and the art market collapsed. he died in 1675, aged 43, leaving his family deep in debt. he used costly natural ultramarine, ground from lapis lazuli, even in shadows. key works include the milkmaid (about 1657 to 1658), view of delft (about 1660 to 1661) and girl with a pearl earring (about 1665). some features of his paintings have led scholars to argue that he used a camera obscura. the question remains debated. in the 1860s the critic théophile thoré-bürger rediscovered him. in the 1940s han van meegeren sold a fake vermeer to hermann göring. a 2023 rijksmuseum exhibition of 28 of his works sold out within days.

title: John Curtin
sum: John Curtin (1885 to 1945) was Prime Minister of Australia from 1941 to 1945, leading the country through the Pacific war against Japan during the Second World War.
search: john curtin john curtin (1885 to 1945) was prime minister of australia from 1941 to 1945, leading the country through the pacific war against japan during the second world war. a former journalist and trade unionist who had opposed conscription during the first world war, he became labor party leader in 1935 and prime minister in october 1941. after japan entered the war in december 1941 and bombed darwin in february 1942, he redirected australian forces from the european theatre and, over british objections, recalled australian troops from the middle east to defend against japanese advance. he committed australia more closely to the united states for wartime defense, stating in december 1941 that australia looked to america "free of any pangs" about its traditional ties to britain. he introduced wartime economic controls and expanded the australian government's role in social welfare, but died in office in july 1945, weeks before japan's surrender, worn down by the strain of the war years.

title: José Martí
sum: José Martí (1853 to 1895) was a Cuban poet, journalist and organizer who founded the Cuban Revolutionary Party in 1892 and helped launch the 1895 war of independence against Spain. He was killed in one of its first battles.
search: josé martí josé martí (1853 to 1895) was a cuban poet, journalist and organizer who founded the cuban revolutionary party in 1892 and helped launch the 1895 war of independence against spain. he was killed in one of its first battles. martí was born in havana on 28 january 1853. arrested at 16 over a letter criticizing a schoolmate who joined the spanish army, he was sentenced to six years' hard labor and deported to spain in 1871. he later lived in mexico, guatemala, venezuela and, from 1880, mainly new york. he published ismaelillo (1882), versos sencillos (1891) and the essay "nuestra américa" (1891), which argued that latin american countries should govern from knowledge of their own peoples. in 1892 he founded the cuban revolutionary party and its newspaper patria, arguing for a republic open to all races and against united states expansion into cuba. he landed in eastern cuba on 11 april 1895 and was killed at dos ríos on 19 may in his first engagement. cuba became formally independent in 1902, under limits set by the united states. both the cuban government and cuban exile groups have since claimed him as a symbol.

title: José María Velasco
sum: José María Velasco (6 July 1840 to 26 August 1912) was the most important Mexican painter of the 19th century, known for panoramic views of the Valley of Mexico. He was also a trained naturalist who illustrated scientific publications on…
search: josé maría velasco josé maría velasco (6 july 1840 to 26 august 1912) was the most important mexican painter of the 19th century, known for panoramic views of the valley of mexico. he was also a trained naturalist who illustrated scientific publications on botany, zoology and geology. velasco was born in temascalcingo, in the state of mexico. his family moved to mexico city in 1849. in 1858 he entered the academy of san carlos, where the italian painter eugenio landesio taught him to observe nature closely and paint outdoors. he also studied botany, zoology, anatomy, physics and mathematics. in 1877 he succeeded landesio as professor of landscape painting. among his students was diego rivera. he worked as a scientific illustrator for the national museum and on expeditions, and painted archaeological sites such as teotihuacan. he won a medal at the paris universal exposition of 1889 and exhibited at the 1893 chicago world's columbian exposition. one view of the valley of mexico was given to pope leo xiii and is now in the vatican museums. he worked from outdoor sketches to large studio compositions. his panoramas set a detailed foreground of cacti and rocks against a luminous distance, and often include railways, bridges and haciendas alongside nature and ruins. key works include the valley of mexico from the santa isabel mountain range (1875), the pyramid of the sun at teotihuacan (1878) and the curved bridge over the metlac ravine (1881). he died in mexico city during the early years of the mexican revolution. his views record lakes and open plains since swallowed by mexico city. the museo josé maría velasco in toluca opened in 1992.

title: José Rizal
sum: José Rizal (1861 to 1896) was a Filipino physician, writer and reformer whose novels criticized Spanish colonial rule. Spanish authorities executed him in Manila on 30 December 1896, and he is regarded as a national hero of the Philippines.
search: josé rizal josé rizal (1861 to 1896) was a filipino physician, writer and reformer whose novels criticized spanish colonial rule. spanish authorities executed him in manila on 30 december 1896, and he is regarded as a national hero of the philippines. rizal was born on 19 june 1861 in calamba, in the philippines. he studied in manila, madrid, paris and heidelberg and became an eye doctor. he wrote the novels noli me tángere (1887) and el filibusterismo (1891), which portrayed abuses by spanish friars and officials; the colonial authorities banned them. in 1892 he founded la liga filipina, a reform society, and was exiled to dapitan on mindanao, where he practiced medicine and taught until 1896. the philippine revolution began in august 1896. rizal, who had volunteered as a doctor in cuba, was arrested on his way there, brought back to manila and convicted of rebellion. he had said he opposed an armed uprising at that time. he was shot by firing squad on 30 december 1896, aged 35. before his death he wrote a poem now known as "mi último adiós."

title: João III
sum: João III (1502 to 1557) was King of Portugal from 1521 to 1557, presiding over the height of Portugal's Asian trading empire while also introducing the Inquisition and formal colonization of Brazil.
search: joão iii joão iii (1502 to 1557) was king of portugal from 1521 to 1557, presiding over the height of portugal's asian trading empire while also introducing the inquisition and formal colonization of brazil. under his reign portuguese trading posts and fortresses across the indian ocean, from east africa to goa, malacca and macau, reached their fullest extent, built on the routes opened by earlier explorers such as vasco da gama. he introduced the portuguese inquisition in 1536, targeting jewish converts (new christians) suspected of secretly practicing judaism, at the urging of factions at his court and with eventual papal approval. he divided brazil into hereditary captaincies from 1534 to encourage settlement and defense of the colony, a system that had mixed results and was later partly replaced by direct royal government. he was a patron of portuguese scholarship, moving the university at lisbon to coimbra in 1537, but the enormous cost of maintaining the asian trading empire strained the crown's finances by the end of his reign.

title: Kamehameha I
sum: Kamehameha I (about 1750 to 1819) was a chief of Hawaiʻi Island who united the Hawaiian Islands under one rule by 1810, founding the Kingdom of Hawaiʻi, whose last monarch was Liliuokalani.
search: kamehameha i kamehameha i (about 1750 to 1819) was a chief of hawaiʻi island who united the hawaiian islands under one rule by 1810, founding the kingdom of hawaiʻi, whose last monarch was liliuokalani. kamehameha was born at kohala on hawaiʻi island. estimates of his birth year range from 1736 to 1761. he died on 8 may 1819, though some sources say 14 may. after his uncle, the ruler kalaniʻōpuʻu, died in 1782, he became guardian of the war god kūkaʻilimoku and defeated his cousin kīwalaʻō at the battle of mokuʻōhai, gaining hawaiʻi island after years of war. he used western firearms and cannon and advisers such as john young and isaac davis. in 1795 he invaded oʻahu, and at nuʻuanu hundreds of defenders were driven over the pali cliff. in 1810 kauaʻi and niʻihau came under his authority by negotiation with their ruler kaumualiʻi, who stayed on as a tributary king. the law of the splintered paddle (māmalahoe kānāwai), protecting noncombatants, is said to come from a 1782 incident in which fishermen struck him with a paddle. his son liholiho succeeded him as kamehameha ii. his burial place was hidden by custom and is unknown.

title: Kate Sheppard
sum: Kate Sheppard (1848 to 1934) was an English-born campaigner who led the movement for women's suffrage in New Zealand. The Electoral Act of 1893 made New Zealand the first self-governing country in which women voted in national elections.
search: kate sheppard kate sheppard (1848 to 1934) was an english-born campaigner who led the movement for women's suffrage in new zealand. the electoral act of 1893 made new zealand the first self-governing country in which women voted in national elections. sheppard was born on 10 march 1848 in liverpool, england, and emigrated to new zealand, arriving in 1869. she died in christchurch on 13 july 1934. from 1887 she was national superintendent for franchise and legislation of the women's christian temperance union, which made votes for women a central aim. petitions to parliament carried about 10,000 signatures in 1891, about 20,000 in 1892 and 31,872 in 1893, the largest petition presented to parliament until then. the governor signed the electoral act on 19 september 1893, and women voted for the first time in the election of 28 november 1893. the act gave the vote to women of all races, including māori women in the māori electorates, but women could not stand for parliament until 1919. her portrait has been on the new zealand ten-dollar note since 1991.

title: Katsushika Hokusai
sum: Katsushika Hokusai (1760 to 1849) was a Japanese ukiyo-e artist from Edo, creator of The Great Wave off Kanagawa. He produced paintings, book illustrations and, in his seventies, the landscape print series that made him world-famous.
search: katsushika hokusai katsushika hokusai (1760 to 1849) was a japanese ukiyo-e artist from edo, creator of the great wave off kanagawa. he produced paintings, book illustrations and, in his seventies, the landscape print series that made him world-famous. hokusai was born in 1760 in the katsushika district of edo (modern tokyo). as a teenager he worked in a lending library and trained as a woodblock carver. about 18 he entered the studio of katsukawa shunshō. he changed his artistic name more than 30 times and is said to have moved house more than 90 times. he lived in poverty for much of his life. his daughter katsushika ōi became a fine painter and assisted him in his old age. in 1814 he began publishing the hokusai manga, fifteen volumes of sketches. about 1830 to 1832 he designed thirty-six views of mount fuji, which includes the great wave off kanagawa (about 1831). in the postscript to one hundred views of mount fuji (1834) he wrote that nothing he drew before age 70 was worth noticing. he died in edo on 10 may 1849, at 88, reportedly saying that with five more years he could have become a true painter. ukiyo-e was a collaborative art: he drew the design, specialist carvers cut it into blocks, one for each colour, and printers pressed the paper by hand. the fuji series used the newly imported prussian blue pigment. he learned western perspective from dutch prints available in japan and combined it with japanese flat colour and strong design. after japan opened to trade in the 1850s he became a sensation in europe. monet, degas, van gogh and cassatt learned from him, and debussy put the great wave on the cover of la mer. the 1,000-yen note issued in 2024 carries the wave, and the sumida hokusai museum opened in tokyo in 2016.

title: Khadija bint Khuwaylid
sum: Khadija bint Khuwaylid (about 555 to 619) was a merchant of Mecca and the first wife of Muhammad. Her dates and many details come from Muslim biographies written more than a century after her death.
search: khadija bint khuwaylid khadija bint khuwaylid (about 555 to 619) was a merchant of mecca and the first wife of muhammad. her dates and many details come from muslim biographies written more than a century after her death. khadija belonged to the quraysh tribe of mecca and, according to tradition, financed trading caravans to syria and hired agents to lead them. tradition says muhammad led one of her caravans and that she proposed marriage, about 595. accounts differ on her age then, and a common figure is 40. muslim tradition holds that she was the first person to accept muhammad's message after his first revelation, about 610. tradition names four daughters, including fatima, and sons who died young. she died about 619, shortly before muhammad's move to medina in 622, a year remembered as the year of sorrow. the earliest biographies, by ibn ishaq and ibn saʿd, were written in the 8th and 9th centuries.

title: Knud Rasmussen
sum: Knud Rasmussen (1879 to 1933) was a Danish-Greenlandic explorer and ethnographer who recorded Inuit oral traditions and led the Fifth Thule Expedition (1921 to 1924), a dog-sled journey from Greenland across Arctic Canada to Alaska.
search: knud rasmussen knud rasmussen (1879 to 1933) was a danish-greenlandic explorer and ethnographer who recorded inuit oral traditions and led the fifth thule expedition (1921 to 1924), a dog-sled journey from greenland across arctic canada to alaska. knud rasmussen was born on 7 june 1879 in jakobshavn (ilulissat), greenland, to a danish missionary father and a mother of part greenlandic inuit descent, and grew up speaking greenlandic. in 1910 he and peter freuchen founded the thule trading station at cape york in northwest greenland, which helped fund his expeditions. on the fifth thule expedition he traveled with greenlandic inuit companions across northern canada to alaska. the expedition's archaeologist, therkel mathiassen, excavated sites that led to the identification of the thule culture. he collected songs, stories and accounts of belief from the iglulik and other inuit groups, and wrote  across arctic america  (1927). he fell ill on the seventh thule expedition and died in copenhagen on 21 december 1933.

title: Kristina of Sweden
sum: Kristina (1626 to 1689) was Queen of Sweden from 1632 to 1654, known for her patronage of scholars and the arts, her unexpected abdication, and her secret conversion to Catholicism in a firmly Protestant kingdom.
search: kristina of sweden kristina (1626 to 1689) was queen of sweden from 1632 to 1654, known for her patronage of scholars and the arts, her unexpected abdication, and her secret conversion to catholicism in a firmly protestant kingdom. she became queen at age five after her father gustavus adolphus died in battle, ruling under a regency until she assumed full power in 1644. she invited scholars including rene descartes to her court in stockholm; descartes died there in 1650, reportedly worn down by the early-morning hours she kept for their lessons. she abdicated the throne in 1654 in favor of her cousin, and after leaving sweden she converted to catholicism in secret in brussels in december 1654, a decision scandalous in lutheran sweden that she announced publicly in 1655. she spent most of her later life in rome under the pope's protection, becoming a prominent patron of music and art, and was one of very few women buried in st. peter's basilica.

title: Kupe
sum: Kupe is a legendary Polynesian navigator credited in Maori oral tradition with being the first to reach and name Aotearoa (New Zealand); no fixed historical date can be assigned to him.
search: kupe kupe is a legendary polynesian navigator credited in maori oral tradition with being the first to reach and name aotearoa (new zealand); no fixed historical date can be assigned to him. traditions describe kupe sailing from the ancestral homeland hawaiki, in some versions pursuing the giant octopus te wheke-a-muturangi, and reaching the north island of new zealand. he is credited with naming numerous coastal landmarks, several of which are still used today, and with returning to hawaiki afterward to describe the land he had found. different iwi (tribal) traditions place him at varying points, and 19th- and 20th-century european writers synthesized these into a single traditional date of roughly 925 ce (the orthodox version tied to s. percy smith; other sources give about 900 to 1200 ce) that many historians now treat with caution. no archaeological or written record fixes kupe's voyage; the earliest confirmed archaeological evidence for human settlement of new zealand dates to around the 13th century ce, later than most traditional accounts imply.

title: Lady Six Sky
sum: Lady Six Sky (Wak Chanil Ajaw; active 682 to 741 CE) was a Maya noblewoman from Dos Pilas who arrived at Naranjo in 682 and effectively ruled the city for decades, restoring it after a period of defeat.
search: lady six sky lady six sky (wak chanil ajaw; active 682 to 741 ce) was a maya noblewoman from dos pilas who arrived at naranjo in 682 and effectively ruled the city for decades, restoring it after a period of defeat. she was a daughter of the dos pilas king b'alaj chan k'awiil, part of a network of the powerful city of calakmul's allies against its rival tikal. naranjo's royal line had been broken after a defeat by caracol, and lady six sky was installed there in 682, apparently to re-establish the dynasty. monuments record her overseeing military campaigns and presiding over her young son k'ahk' tiliw chan chaahk's accession in 693, after which she continued to appear on inscriptions as a ruling figure into the 700s. she never took the full royal title used by male kings of naranjo, and continued to use the emblem glyph of her home city dos pilas throughout her life, so her exact formal status is debated by epigraphers.

title: Laozi
sum: Laozi (Lao Tzu, "Old Master") is the traditional author of the Daodejing and a founding figure of Daoism, said to have lived in the 6th century BCE. Whether he was a single historical person is disputed.
search: laozi laozi (lao tzu, "old master") is the traditional author of the daodejing and a founding figure of daoism, said to have lived in the 6th century bce. whether he was a single historical person is disputed. laozi is traditionally placed in the 6th century bce, in the time of confucius. the date is uncertain and no date of death is known. the historian sima qian, writing about 100 bce, identifies him as li er, keeper of archives at the zhou court, and also lists other men who might have been meant, so the uncertainty was already old. sima qian's account says he met confucius, then left the zhou domain to the west and wrote the text at the hangu pass at the request of the gatekeeper yin xi. this account is traditional. the daodejing has about 5,000 chinese characters in 81 short chapters. its earliest excavated versions, from guodian (about 300 bce) and mawangdui (tomb sealed 168 bce), fit the view of most scholars that the text took shape in the 4th to 3rd centuries bce. later religious daoism honored him as a deity, laojun, and the tang dynasty's imperial family, named li, claimed him as an ancestor.

title: Lautaro
sum: Lautaro (about 1534 to 1557) was a Mapuche toqui, or war leader (described at Tucapel as a vice toqui under the supreme toqui Caupolicán), who organized effective resistance to Spanish conquest in what is now southern Chile, after years…
search: lautaro lautaro (about 1534 to 1557) was a mapuche toqui, or war leader (described at tucapel as a vice toqui under the supreme toqui caupolicán), who organized effective resistance to spanish conquest in what is now southern chile, after years spent as a captured servant in the spanish camp. as a young captive, he served the spanish conquistador pedro de valdivia and observed spanish tactics, horsemanship and weapons before escaping back to his people. he introduced cavalry tactics, relay messenger systems and coordinated ambushes to mapuche warfare, adapting methods he had learned from the spanish. in december 1553 his forces, serving under the supreme toqui caupolicán, defeated a spanish column at the battle of tucapel, where valdivia was captured and killed (sources differ on the details of his death), a major blow to the early spanish conquest of chile. he was killed in a surprise spanish attack on his camp at the mataquito river in april 1557, ending a campaign that had held spanish expansion south of the bio-bio river in check for years.

title: Leo Tolstoy
sum: Leo Tolstoy (1828 to 1910) was a Russian novelist, author of the realist epics War and Peace and Anna Karenina. A religious crisis in the second half of his life turned him toward shorter fiction and writing on faith, mortality and…
search: leo tolstoy leo tolstoy (1828 to 1910) was a russian novelist, author of the realist epics war and peace and anna karenina. a religious crisis in the second half of his life turned him toward shorter fiction and writing on faith, mortality and nonviolence that influenced gandhi. tolstoy was born in 1828 into an aristocratic family at yasnaya polyana, the estate south of moscow he inherited and managed for most of his life. he served briefly as an army officer in the crimean war. in the 1860s and 1870s he wrote war and peace (1869) and anna karenina (1877), and founded a school for the children on his estate. after anna karenina he underwent a spiritual crisis, described in a confession. he rejected the russian orthodox church, embraced an ascetic, pacifist reading of christian ethics and increasingly disowned his earlier fiction as morally frivolous. his later works include the death of ivan ilyich (1886), the kreutzer sonata (1889) and resurrection (1899), shorter, starker and more didactic than the novels. war and peace argues in long digressions that the forces driving historical events lay far beyond the control of any single general or emperor. his writing on nonviolent resistance to evil directly influenced mahatma gandhi, who corresponded with him near the end of his life. he died in 1910 of pneumonia at a remote railway station, after collapsing on a flight from his estate. yasnaya polyana is preserved as a museum.

title: Leonardo da Vinci
sum: Leonardo da Vinci (15 April 1452 to 2 May 1519) was an Italian painter, engineer and anatomist. He left few finished paintings, with counts differing but fewer than 25 attributed major works, some of them unfinished, including the Mona…
search: leonardo da vinci leonardo da vinci (15 april 1452 to 2 may 1519) was an italian painter, engineer and anatomist. he left few finished paintings, with counts differing but fewer than 25 attributed major works, some of them unfinished, including the mona lisa and the last supper, and thousands of notebook pages of studies. leonardo was born on 15 april 1452 near vinci in tuscany, the illegitimate son of a notary, ser piero, and a young woman named caterina. he was apprenticed in florence to andrea del verrocchio. about 1482 he moved to milan. in a letter to duke ludovico sforza he stressed his skills as a military engineer before his art. in milan he painted the last supper. after the french invaded milan in 1499 he moved between mantua, venice and florence, worked briefly as a military engineer for cesare borgia, and in florence began the mona lisa. in 1516 king francis i invited him to france and gave him the manor of clos lucé near amboise. he died there on 2 may 1519. his pupil francesco melzi inherited his paintings, tools, library and personal effects, and by tradition his notebooks. his notebooks hold thousands of pages of drawings and mirror-writing, with studies of anatomy, flight, hydraulics and optics. he dissected corpses to understand muscles and bones. he pioneered sfumato, soft modelling without hard outlines. key works include the virgin of the rocks (about 1483 to 1493, sources differ), lady with an ermine (about 1489 to 1491), vitruvian man (about 1485 to 1490, sources differ), the last supper (about 1495 to 1498) and the mona lisa (about 1503 to 1519). his experiments with materials sometimes failed: the last supper began to decay within decades. the codex leicester was bought by bill gates in 1994. in 2017 the salvator mundi, attributed to leonardo, sold for $450 million, a record for a painting; its attribution remains disputed.

title: Li Qingzhao

search: li qingzhao li qingzhao (1084 to about 1155) was a chinese poet of the song dynasty, widely regarded as the greatest woman writer in the classical chinese tradition. her ci, a lyric verse form, moved from a settled, cultured life to loss and exile after northern china fell to invaders. she was born in 1084 in qi prefecture, today's zhangqiu in shandong, to a literary family, and is thought to have died about 1155. in 1101 she married zhao mingcheng, a scholar who shared her interest in antiquities. the jinshi lu, a catalog of bronze and stone inscriptions, is described as her husband's work and was published after his death. when the jin dynasty invaded northern china in 1127, the couple fled south with part of their collection, much of which is said to have been lost along the way. zhao mingcheng died in 1129. after his death she wrote an afterword to the jinshi lu describing their marriage and their losses. she briefly remarried, with the year traditionally given as about 1132, and divorced amid scandal soon after. her poems, mostly short ci in personal, direct language, describe love, separation, and later grief and displacement. only around a hundred of her poems are known to survive, out of a larger body assembled and praised by later editors.

title: Liliuokalani
sum: Liliuokalani (1838 to 1917) was the last monarch of the Kingdom of Hawaii, reigning from 1891 until she was deposed in January 1893 by a group of residents backed by United States troops.
search: liliuokalani liliuokalani (1838 to 1917) was the last monarch of the kingdom of hawaii, reigning from 1891 until she was deposed in january 1893 by a group of residents backed by united states troops. liliuokalani was born in honolulu on 2 september 1838 and died there on 11 november 1917. she succeeded her brother kalākaua on 29 january 1891 and was the kingdom's only reigning queen. in january 1893 she moved to issue a constitution restoring royal powers reduced by the 1887 "bayonet constitution." on 17 january 1893 a committee of safety of mostly american and european residents overthrew her while united states marines were ashore. she yielded to the united states government to avoid bloodshed and asked it to reinstate her. after a failed royalist uprising she was arrested and signed an abdication in january 1895. native hawaiians submitted mass petitions against annexation in 1897, and the united states annexed hawaii in 1898. she composed songs, including "aloha ʻoe," and published a memoir,  hawaii's story by hawaii's queen , in 1898. in 1993 the united states congress apologized to native hawaiians for the overthrow, carried out with the participation of agents and citizens of the united states.

title: Louis Comfort Tiffany
sum: Louis Comfort Tiffany (1848 to 1933) was an American designer whose iridescent Favrile glass, stained-glass windows and lamps became the signature look of American Art Nouveau. Recent scholarship credits many of his studio's best-known…
search: louis comfort tiffany louis comfort tiffany (1848 to 1933) was an american designer whose iridescent favrile glass, stained-glass windows and lamps became the signature look of american art nouveau. recent scholarship credits many of his studio's best-known designs to staff designers, above all clara driscoll. tiffany was born in new york in 1848, the son of the jeweller charles lewis tiffany. he trained as a painter under george inness before turning to interior design and decorative arts in the 1870s. his firm redecorated state rooms in the white house in 1882 for president chester arthur; the work was later removed. in 1885 he founded what became tiffany studios, and in 1894 he trademarked the name favrile. his byzantine-style chapel for the 1893 world's columbian exposition in chicago won international acclaim. he built laurelton hall on long island as a showcase of his work. favrile glass builds iridescent, metallic colour into molten glass through mineral oxides. "drapery glass" was manipulated while hot to form folds like fabric. financial losses, traced back to the 1920s and continuing into the depression, forced the studio's closure. he died in new york in 1933. much of the detailed design of individual pieces, especially the lamps, was done by staff designers, above all clara driscoll, who led the women's glass-cutting department. for most of the 20th century tiffany was credited as sole designer. the mid-2000s rediscovery of driscoll's letters credited her and the women of the "tiffany girls" department with several famous lamps, including the dragonfly, a correction now generally accepted by museums and scholars.

title: Ludwig II
sum: Ludwig II (1845 to 1886), sometimes called the "Fairy Tale King," was King of Bavaria from 1864 until his death, remembered for building extravagant romantic castles and for his patronage of the composer Richard Wagner.
search: ludwig ii ludwig ii (1845 to 1886), sometimes called the "fairy tale king," was king of bavaria from 1864 until his death, remembered for building extravagant romantic castles and for his patronage of the composer richard wagner. he became an early and enthusiastic patron of richard wagner, paying off the composer's debts and funding productions, though political opposition to wagner's influence at court eventually forced the composer to leave munich. he commissioned several elaborate castles, most famously neuschwanstein, begun in 1869 and inspired partly by wagner's operas; the castles were funded from his personal fortune rather than the bavarian state treasury but still left him deeply in debt. bavaria's defeat alongside austria in the 1866 austro-prussian war, and its incorporation into the german empire in 1871, steadily reduced his practical political authority even as he retained the throne. in 1886 a government commission, citing his mounting debts and reclusive behavior, had him declared mentally unfit to rule; he died under unclear circumstances in lake starnberg the day after being confined, an event still debated as accident, suicide, or possible foul play.

title: Lumière Brothers
sum: Auguste Lumière (1862 to 1954) and Louis Lumière (1864 to 1948) were French manufacturers of photographic plates who patented the Cinématographe in 1895 and staged the first paying public screening of projected motion pictures. The dates…
search: lumière brothers auguste lumière (1862 to 1954) and louis lumière (1864 to 1948) were french manufacturers of photographic plates who patented the cinématographe in 1895 and staged the first paying public screening of projected motion pictures. the dates here run from auguste's birth to his death. the brothers were born in besançon and grew up in lyon, where their father antoine ran a portrait studio and later a factory making dry photographic plates. after their father saw a demonstration of edison's single-viewer kinetoscope in 1894, they set out to build a device that could project moving images to a seated audience. louis is generally credited with the key mechanical insight, adapting the sewing machine's intermittent claw movement to advance the film. they patented the cinématographe in february 1895, one device that could shoot, print and project. their first paying public screening was on 28 december 1895 in the salon indien of the grand café in paris, traditionally described as a basement on the boulevard des capucines: ten short films for roughly thirty-five to forty people, though accounts differ. their "actuality" films were usually a single static, unedited shot of under a minute. l'arroseur arrosé is a rare staged gag, effectively cinema's first fiction film. key works include workers leaving the lumière factory (1895) and the arrival of a train at la ciotat (1896). they sent camera operators around the world, spreading projected cinema to india, japan, australia and the americas within a year or two. by 1905, about a decade after the first screening, they had largely withdrawn from film production. in 1907 they introduced the autochrome, an early commercially successful colour photography process.

title: Mahatma Gandhi

title: Malinche

title: Mary Cassatt

search: mary cassatt mary cassatt (22 may 1844 to 14 june 1926) was an american painter who spent most of her adult life in france and was the only american to exhibit with the french impressionists. she is celebrated for tender, unsentimental images of women and children. cassatt was born in allegheny city, now part of pittsburgh, into a wealthy family. against her father's wishes she studied at the pennsylvania academy of the fine arts from about 1860, then left for paris in 1866. women could not enter the école des beaux-arts, so she studied privately and copied old masters in the louvre. frustrated with the salon's conservative taste, she accepted degas's invitation in 1877 to exhibit with the impressionists, and showed with them in 1879, 1880, 1881 and 1886. her parents and sister moved to paris to live with her, and her family became her favourite models. in 1890 an exhibition of japanese prints in paris inspired a set of colour prints, usually counted as ten, combining drypoint and aquatint. she took from them flat colour, strong outlines and cropped compositions. in 1893 she painted the mural modern woman for the woman's building at the chicago world's columbian exposition; it has been lost. she advised louisine havemeyer and other americans on buying impressionists and, according to some sources, old masters, many now in the metropolitan museum. she supported the women's suffrage movement. failing eyesight forced her to stop working about 1914. key works include little girl in a blue armchair (1878), the child's bath (1893) and the boating party (1893 to 1894).

search: mimar sinan mimar sinan (about 1489 to 1588) was chief royal architect to three ottoman sultans for nearly fifty years. he is credited with several hundred structures, and his selimiye mosque at edirne is regarded as the peak of classical ottoman architecture. sinan was born about 1489 or 1490 in ağırnas, near kayseri in central anatolia, into a christian family. sources disagree on whether it was greek or armenian. he was conscripted through the devşirme levy into the ottoman elite corps, converted to islam and trained as a janissary. he rose through military engineering, building bridges and fortifications on campaign for suleiman the magnificent. chelebi lütfi pasha appointed him chief royal architect in 1539, when he became grand vizier, a post sinan held into his late nineties. he died in istanbul in 1588. his main buildings are the şehzade mosque (1543 to 1548), the süleymaniye mosque (1550 to 1557) and the selimiye mosque (1568 or 1569 to 1574 or 1575). he described them as his apprenticeship, journeyman work and masterpiece. he worked to build domes wider and more daring than hagia sophia, a byzantine cathedral converted to a mosque after 1453, using semi-domes, buttressing piers and pendentives. he also built aqueducts and bridges, some still in use. he trained a generation of students. turkey's largest architecture prize carries his name, and the selimiye mosque was inscribed as a unesco world heritage site in 2011.

search: mirabai mirabai (traditionally about 1498 to about 1546) was a rajput princess from rajasthan and one of the best-known poet-saints of the bhakti movement, devoted to krishna. almost nothing about her life is documented, and the surviving poems were written down long after her time. by tradition mirabai was born about 1498 at kudki in rajasthan, into the rathore rajput family of merta, and died about 1546 or 1547. both dates come from later tradition. tradition says she married bhoj raj, heir of mewar, in 1516, and that he died about 1521 of battle wounds. her poems (padas) are in rajasthani and related hindi, and address krishna in the language of love and separation. tradition credits her with a very large number of poems. scholars think only a few hundred may be authentic, and only two are known from manuscripts older than the early eighteenth century. stories that her in-laws tried to poison her, and that she vanished into an image of krishna, are hagiographic legends. the earliest records, from the seventeenth century, do not mention her marriage or in-laws.

title: Montezuma II

search: montezuma ii montezuma ii (moctezuma; about 1466 to 1520) was the ninth ruler (tlatoani) of the aztec empire, reigning at its greatest territorial extent until the arrival of hernan cortes and the spanish conquest. he extended aztec control through further conquests mainly in oaxaca and guerrero, plus a campaign around 1514 through the huastec region, and reorganized the empire's tribute and administrative systems. cortes and a small spanish force reached the capital tenochtitlan in november 1519; montezuma received them and was subsequently held as a hostage within his own palace. accounts of his final months differ: spanish sources say he tried to calm his people during the fighting that followed the 1520 toxcatl massacre and cortes's return, and was killed by a stone thrown by his own subjects, while some later aztec-descended chroniclers say the spanish killed him directly. his death in june 1520 came shortly before the spanish were driven from the city in the "noche triste"; his brother cuitlahuac and then his nephew cuauhtemoc took up the resistance that ended with tenochtitlan's fall in 1521.

search: muhammad ali of egypt muhammad ali, an ottoman officer of albanian family, became governor of egypt in 1805, destroyed the old mamluk elite, built a conscript army and state-run economy, and founded the dynasty that ruled egypt until 1952. muhammad ali was born in kavala, in what is now greece, to an albanian family from the korçë region. his father was a tobacco merchant and an ottoman military commander. he rose to power after the french withdrawal from egypt in 1801. in 1805 prominent egyptians, including the religious scholars, demanded his appointment as governor (wali), and the ottomans accepted. in 1811 he invited the leading mamluks to a celebration at the cairo citadel, where his forces ambushed and killed them. more mamluks were then hunted down in cairo and elsewhere, for a total of perhaps 3,000. he introduced long-staple cotton, built an army of conscripts trained by european officers, and set up a state-run industrial economy. he founded the dynasty that ruled egypt until 1952.

"murasaki shikibu" is a later nickname. her personal name is unknown; the nickname combines a character from her novel with her father's court rank. she was born about 973 into a minor branch of the fujiwara clan and learned the chinese classics, normally reserved for men, by absorbing lessons given to her brother. she married a much older provincial governor about 998 and was widowed within a few years. about 1005 or 1006 she entered court service as a lady-in-waiting to empress shōshi. the tale of genji follows a fictional prince and, in its later chapters, his descendants. it may have been begun before she came to court, though sources suggest she likely composed it while serving as a lady-in-waiting, possibly chapter by chapter. she wrote almost entirely in hiragana, the script associated with women's writing at court, and set many waka poems into the story as the characters' own compositions. she also kept the diary of lady murasaki, which records court life and rivalries. she is thought to have died about 1014; the date, like most of her biography, is uncertain. the earliest surviving illustrated version, the 12th-century genji monogatari emaki, is a japanese national treasure. she appears on the 2000 yen banknote.

title: Nefertiti

search: nefertiti nefertiti (about 1370 to about 1330 bce) was the great royal wife of the egyptian king akhenaten and is shown with unusual prominence in the art of his reign. her exact birth and death dates and her burial place are uncertain, and the dates given are approximate. nefertiti married akhenaten (then amenhotep iv) early in his reign; the exact dates of the marriage are uncertain. the couple promoted the worship of the sun disk aten and moved the royal capital to a new city, akhetaten (modern amarna). reliefs and statues show nefertiti at a scale and in roles usually reserved for the king, including taking part in rites for the aten. they had six daughters, including meritaten and ankhesenamun, who later married tutankhamun. scholarship before 2012 assumed she vanished from the record around year 12 of the reign, but an inscription dated to year 16 names neferneferuaten-nefertiti alongside akhenaten. whether she died, changed title, or ruled as co-regent under the name neferneferuaten is debated. a painted limestone bust found in 1912 in the workshop of the sculptor thutmose at amarna is held in berlin; egypt has requested its return. later king lists omitted akhenaten and his immediate successors.

title: Nelson Mandela

title: Nezahualcoyotl
sum: Nezahualcoyotl (1402 to 1472) was the tlatoani, or ruler, of the Acolhua city-state of Texcoco in the Valley of Mexico and a founder of the Triple Alliance with Tenochtitlan and Tlacopan. He is remembered as a lawgiver, builder and poet,…

title: Nur Jahan
sum: Nur Jahan (1577 to 1645) was a Mughal empress and the wife of the emperor Jahangir, who held great political power at court from about 1611 to 1627.

title: Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba

title: Pachacuti

title: Pedro II
sum: Pedro II (1825 to 1891) was Emperor of Brazil from 1831 to 1889, presiding over six decades of relative political stability, territorial integrity, and gradual abolition of slavery before being deposed in a republican coup.
search: pedro ii pedro ii (1825 to 1891) was emperor of brazil from 1831 to 1889, presiding over six decades of relative political stability, territorial integrity, and gradual abolition of slavery before being deposed in a republican coup. he became emperor at age five after his father abdicated, ruling under regents until being declared of age early, in 1840, to stabilize a period of regional revolts. his government fought the paraguayan war from 1864 to 1870 alongside argentina and uruguay, the deadliest interstate war in latin american history, which devastated paraguay's population. he personally supported gradual abolition of slavery, and his daughter and regent, princess isabel, signed the golden law abolishing slavery outright in 1888, the last country in the americas to do so. brazilian military officers, landowners angered by abolition, and republican advocates combined to depose him in a bloodless coup in november 1889, ending the monarchy and sending him into exile in europe, where he died in 1891.

title: Pericles
sum: Pericles (about 495 to 429 BCE) was the leading Athenian statesman for over three decades in the mid-5th century BCE, a period later called the Golden Age of Athens for its building programs, drama, and democratic institutions.
search: pericles pericles (about 495 to 429 bce) was the leading athenian statesman for over three decades in the mid-5th century bce, a period later called the golden age of athens for its building programs, drama, and democratic institutions. he rose to prominence in athenian democracy through the office of strategos (general), to which he was re-elected yearly, using his influence over the assembly rather than any formal single office to shape policy. he directed the building program on the acropolis, including the parthenon, funded partly by treasury funds originally collected from the delian league, an alliance of greek states organized against persia. he extended pay for jury service and other public roles to poorer citizens, broadening practical participation in athenian democracy beyond the wealthy. he championed the aggressive strategy that led athens into the peloponnesian war against sparta in 431 bce, and died of plague in 429 bce during the war's early years, before its outcome was decided.

title: Peter the Great
sum: Peter I, called Peter the Great (1672 to 1725), ruled Russia from 1682, jointly at first and alone from 1696, until 1725, driving a sweeping program of westernizing reform and transforming Russia into a major European power.
search: peter the great peter i, called peter the great (1672 to 1725), ruled russia from 1682, jointly at first and alone from 1696, until 1725, driving a sweeping program of westernizing reform and transforming russia into a major european power. he traveled incognito through western europe in 1697 to 1698 on the "grand embassy," working for a time as a shipwright in the netherlands to study european shipbuilding and technology firsthand. he fought a long war against sweden, the great northern war from 1700 to 1721, winning a decisive victory at the battle of poltava in 1709 and gaining territory on the baltic sea that made russia a major naval power. he founded the city of st. petersburg in 1703 on newly won baltic territory, building it as a planned european-style capital and moving the seat of government there from moscow. he reorganized the russian government, military, and church administration along western european lines, and required russian nobles to adopt western dress, in a well-known instance personally cutting off boyars' traditional long beards to symbolize the change.

title: Philip II
sum: Philip II (1527 to 1598) was King of Spain from 1556 to 1598, ruling an empire that spanned the Iberian Peninsula, the Netherlands, parts of Italy, and vast territories in the Americas and the Philippines, which were named after him.

title: Pieter Bruegel the Elder
sum: Pieter Bruegel the Elder (about 1525 to 1569) was the most important Netherlandish painter of the 16th century. He made peasants, proverbs and the turning seasons his subjects, in crowded panels and sweeping landscapes. Only about 40 of…
search: pieter bruegel the elder pieter bruegel the elder (about 1525 to 1569) was the most important netherlandish painter of the 16th century. he made peasants, proverbs and the turning seasons his subjects, in crowded panels and sweeping landscapes. only about 40 of his paintings survive. bruegel was probably born between 1525 and 1530, perhaps near breda in the duchy of brabant. in 1551 he became a master in the painters' guild of antwerp. in 1552 he travelled to italy. his drawings of the alps on the return journey fed the mountain views of his later paintings. in antwerp he designed prints for the publisher hieronymus cock, some in the manner of hieronymus bosch. in 1563 he married mayken coecke and moved to brussels, where he painted most of his masterpieces. he died in brussels in september 1569. his sons pieter brueghel the younger and jan brueghel the elder became successful painters and founded a dynasty. key works include netherlandish proverbs (1559), children's games (1560), the tower of babel (1563), the hunters in the snow (1565) and the peasant wedding (about 1567 to 1568). he often used a high viewpoint over dozens of small figures, and built pictures around proverbs, games or bible stories retold in flemish dress. he painted during the religious conflicts and spanish repression that led to the dutch revolt. many scholars see hidden commentary on these events in his work. according to the early biographer karel van mander, he and a friend dressed as peasants to join village weddings and fairs. the kunsthistorisches museum in vienna holds the world's largest group of his paintings.

title: Piye
sum: Piye (reigned about 744 to 714 BCE) was a king of Kush who conquered Egypt and is usually counted as the first ruler of Egypt's Twenty-fifth (Kushite) Dynasty. His birth year is unknown; the dates given here are those of his reign.
search: piye piye (reigned about 744 to 714 bce) was a king of kush who conquered egypt and is usually counted as the first ruler of egypt's twenty-fifth (kushite) dynasty. his birth year is unknown; the dates given here are those of his reign. piye ruled kush from napata, near jebel barkal in present-day sudan. his reign is dated about 744 to 714 bce; some scholars count his father kashta as the dynasty's first ruler. about 728 bce he marched north against tefnakht, prince of sais, and a coalition of delta rulers, and defeated them. his victory stele, found at jebel barkal in 1862 and now in cairo, records the campaign in egyptian hieroglyphs, presents him as serving the god amun, and lists the rulers who submitted to him. he did not remain in egypt; he returned to kush and left local rulers in place. he expanded the temple of amun at jebel barkal. he was buried in a pyramid at el-kurru, with horses. he was succeeded by shebitku, whom sources describe as either his son or his brother; recent evidence places shabaka's reign after shebitku's, not before.

title: Qin Shi Huang
sum: Qin Shi Huang (259 to 210 BCE) was the first emperor of a unified China, who standardized writing, currency, and measures and built a large tomb complex including the terracotta army.

title: Queen Amina of Zazzau
sum: Queen Amina of Zazzau is a traditional figure said to have ruled Zazzau (Zaria), a Hausa state in present-day northern Nigeria, for about 34 years around the turn of the 16th and 17th centuries. She is known from later tradition, and her…
search: queen amina of zazzau queen amina of zazzau is a traditional figure said to have ruled zazzau (zaria), a hausa state in present-day northern nigeria, for about 34 years around the turn of the 16th and 17th centuries. she is known from later tradition, and her dates and status are disputed. some sources give amina's reign as 1576 to 1610; her birth and death years are uncertain (some accounts give 1533 and 1610), and the dates here are those of the reign. whether she held the title of queen is disputed, and she does not appear on the regnal lists. some scholars instead place her in the early to mid fifteenth century, because the kano chronicle calls her a contemporary of muhammad dauda, who ruled from 1421 to 1438. much of what is known comes from the kano chronicle, a late 19th-century compilation of older oral tradition, and from muhammad bello's history infaq al-maysur (dated to 1812 or to about 1836, sources differ), written more than two centuries later. tradition says she led zazzau's army, expanded its territory, and increased its wealth through control of trade routes. earthen walls around hausa towns are traditionally attributed to her. scholars generally accept that she existed, but the details of her life come from tradition. she is remembered in northern nigeria as a warrior queen.

search: queen suriyothai queen suriyothai was a consort of king maha chakkraphat of the ayutthaya kingdom, in present-day thailand, traditionally said to have died in 1548 defending her husband on elephant-back during a burmese invasion. her birth year is traditionally given as 1511, and her story rests on siamese chronicles alone. she was a consort of maha chakkraphat, who became king of ayutthaya in 1546 or 1548, as sources differ. in 1548 the burmese king tabinshwehti invaded ayutthaya. siamese chronicles say suriyothai, disguised and riding an elephant, placed herself between her husband and an enemy commander and was killed by his blow. no burmese chronicle records this episode, and her historicity is questioned. thai accounts add that her daughter, princess boromdilok, was also mortally wounded. a memorial stupa, the chedi si suriyothai, was built by maha chakkraphat at wat suan luang sopsawan on the bank of the chao phraya near ayutthaya, and is traditionally associated with the site of her death. thai nationalist commemoration of her grew in the twentieth century, including a widely seen 2001 film.

title: Queen Victoria

search: queen victoria victoria (1819 to 1901) was queen of the united kingdom from 1837 to 1901, the longest-reigning british monarch until elizabeth ii, presiding over a period of industrial growth and imperial expansion later named after her. she became queen at eighteen after the death of her uncle william iv, and married her cousin prince albert of saxe-coburg and gotha in 1840, with whom she had nine children who married into royal families across europe. her reign saw britain's industrial economy expand rapidly and its colonial empire grow substantially, and she was proclaimed empress of india in 1876. after albert's death in 1861 she withdrew from public life for years, a long seclusion that made her briefly unpopular before she gradually resumed public duties. constitutional practice during her reign shifted royal power further toward a largely ceremonial role exercised through elected ministers, even as the monarchy's cultural and symbolic prominence grew.

title: Rachel Carson

title: Raja Ravi Varma

search: raja ravi varma raja ravi varma (29 april 1848 to 2 october 1906) was the most famous indian painter of the 19th century, from the princely state of travancore. he brought european academic oil painting to scenes from the hindu epics, and his mass-produced prints put images of gods and heroines into homes across india. ravi varma was born at kilimanoor, near thiruvananthapuram, into an aristocratic family related to the ruling house. by tradition his uncle, the painter raja raja varma, noticed his talent. at 14 he was taken to the palace under maharaja ayilyam thirunal and learned oil painting partly by watching the european portraitist theodore jensen. a portrait won a prize at the 1873 vienna exhibition, and his work was shown at the 1893 chicago world's columbian exposition, where it won three gold medals. he painted a series of puranic subjects for maharaja sayajirao gaekwad iii of baroda in 1888 to 1890. in 1894 he set up a lithographic press at ghatkopar in bombay, and moved it in 1899 to malavli near lonavala, producing colour prints (oleographs) of deities and heroines that sold in huge numbers. critics accused him of vulgarising sacred subjects. in 1904 the british viceroy awarded him the kaisar-i-hind gold medal. he died at attingal. he combined victorian academic realism with indian subjects and costumes. his heroines were based on real women and staged at dramatic moments. the early filmmaker dadasaheb phalke worked at his press before making india's first feature film in 1913. later nationalist artists of the bengal school, such as abanindranath tagore, rejected his western style. the kerala government's highest art award, the raja ravi varma puraskaram, bears his name.

title: Ramesses II

title: Razia Sultana

title: Rumi

search: rumi rumi (jalal ad-din muhammad rumi, 1207 to 1273) was a persian-language poet and sufi teacher who spent his adult life in konya, in anatolia. his long poem, the masnavi, and his lyric poems are among the most widely read works of persian literature. rumi was born in 1207 in balkh or nearby wakhsh, in present-day afghanistan or tajikistan; sources differ. his family moved west, and he was living in konya, in the seljuk sultanate of rum, by about 1228. he trained as a scholar and preacher like his father, baha ad-din walad, and taught in konya. in 1244 he met a wandering mystic, shams of tabriz. their friendship changed his life, and he began to write poetry. shams disappeared about 1248, and accounts differ, with some saying he was killed and others that he simply moved on. he wrote the masnavi, a long poem in six books, and thousands of lyric poems collected in the divan of shams. he wrote mostly in persian. the masnavi runs to some 25,000 to 27,000 couplets, with counts differing by source, composed over his last decade or so at the request of his disciple husam al-din chalabi, who wrote the verses down as rumi recited them. some later readers called it "the quran in persian". fihi ma fihi ("in it what is in it") is a prose collection of his informal talks to disciples, valued as the clearest record of how he taught. he died in konya on 17 december 1273. his followers founded the mevlevi order, known for a ritual of whirling. loose english adaptations from the late 20th century onward made him, by some measures, one of the best-selling poets in the united states.
